$comment: Authoritative attestation reference for the production publicai-gateway CVM. Fetched at runtime by the /proof page. composeHash was read back from the CVM's RTMR3 event log on 2026-09-18 and cross-checked against the Phala control-plane API; both report 44e4537b. The sub2api image digest is the linux/amd64 child of the cosign-signed proof-v41 index (INDEX 3ab63323) built by publish-tee-images run 35323360240 from commit bb0a76e38; the attestor image is deliberately left at its proof-v20 pin because deploy/attestor carries no change since that release. HOW THE IMAGE DIGEST WAS RESOLVED, stated plainly because proof-v38 got this wrong and took production down for about 15 minutes: resolved with deploy/phala/pin-amd64.sh (parses `imagetools inspect --raw` as JSON, matches on the platform field); re-checked with the same script's --verify mode after editing compose; the index children were listed and read by a human (00b7a80a linux/amd64 vs 7668c692 unknown/unknown attestation-manifest); and the pinned digest was actually docker-pulled and inspected - linux/amd64, entrypoint present, 140 MB - which an attestation-manifest cannot satisfy. VERIFICATION SCOPE: composeHash, the image digests and the build commit were each read back from a live source, and composeHash was cross-checked against two independent ones. The cosign keyless signature was NOT verified locally for this release - cosign is not installed on the release machine - though the signing workflow run succeeded and anyone can verify certificate identity https://github.com/FiiLabs/sub2api/.github/workflows/publish-tee-images.yml@refs/heads/feat/two-sided-market plus the embedded githubWorkflowSha against the sourceCommit below. This release is frontend-only and touches no schema, no ent models and no dependency wiring. It answers the two questions a prospective contributor asks first and which the product previously left unanswered. (1) 'Can you read my own conversations?' - no, and this is a property of the token rather than a promise: a contributor authorization requests only the inference permission, while the permissions that would allow reading Claude Code sessions, the account profile, file upload, MCP servers or API-key minting are deliberately not requested. The contributor dashboard now states this in plain language before the authorize button, with the full permission comparison in the docs; the copy deliberately also states what connecting DOES mean - quota is consumed, a daily cap is available - because describing only what cannot happen reads as evasion. (2) 'How much can I earn?' - the only previous answer was a percentage, which tells nothing to someone who has never counted tokens. A three-row worked example derives earnings for small, medium and large coding tasks from published list prices and the rates already on the page, so a reader can redo the arithmetic; three rows rather than one number so that the dependence on task size is visible, and the existing 'we commit to the rate, not to an amount' line is pinned by test to remain adjacent to it. There is NO schema migration in this release. Verified before rollout: frontend type-check and the full vitest suite (2086 passing, including five new assertions that the privacy note is present, precedes the authorize button, states both what the token can and cannot do, and keeps its link to the verifiable permission list). A full postgres backup was taken and verified immediately beforehand - downloaded from S3, gzip-tested, 110 COPY sections. Earlier in this line: proof-v40 (configurable homepage campaign banner), proof-v39 (per-campaign online-day buckets, new-contributor-only rewards, idle account re-check), proof-v38 (supply incentive rules engine), proof-v37, v36, v35, v34, v33, v32, v31, v29..v15. osImageHash, appId and instanceId are unchanged; the deploy passed --no-dev-os explicitly and the control plane confirms is_dev false after the rollout. This rollout completed in 82 seconds with no incident.
